News.title: Transgender woman who stabbed killer boyfriend to death after meeting in men’s prison is jailed for life
News.content:
BEHIND BARS Transgender woman who stabbed killer boyfriend to death after meeting in men’s prison is jailed for life

A TRANSGENDER woman has been jailed for stabbing her killer boyfriend to death after they met in a men’s prison.

Before transitioning, Aurin Makepeace met Steven Rothwell in the early 2010s, when they were behind bars for wounding and murder.





Rothwell, 41, was found in the bathroom of his home on August 19 last year with a stab wound to the chest.

Chester Crown Court heard that Makepeace fatally stabbed him with a kitchen knife at his flat in Macclesfield, Cheshire, before spending the night.

CCTV from near Rothwell’s flat shows both of them making several trips to a local shop to buy alcohol during her stay.

A jury convicted Makepeace of murder at Chester Crown Court after a three-week trial.

The killer has now been handed a life sentence, with a minimum term of 27 years.

Makepeace, from Prestatyn, north Wales, claimed Rothwell was holding a knife and it accidentally went into his chest when they were “grappling”.

Blood stains were found in the bathroom, shower and kitchen sinks at his flat.

The defendant told the court she was trying to stop him from attacking another man, who he threatened to kill.



The convicted murderer had been told Gary Kuruc had slept with his “sometime girlfriend”, Makepeace said.

Rothwell’s body was found at 10.43pm on August 19. Makepeace had travelled to Prestatyn and called 999 to say: “I killed my boyfriend.”

The killer claimed she was still at the flat and initially said her name was “Luchay” – her middle name – but then said it was “Katie”, the name of Rothwell’s current girlfriend.

Makepeace had already told someone she “killed Steven”, the court heard.

The defendant told another friend: “I’ve murdered my boyfriend.”



Makepeace claimed that she had stabbed him because he had been strangling her.

The killer then drank vodka under a bush, before cops picked her up.

Richard Pratt KC, prosecuting, said Rothwell’s death was “no accident”.

He said Makepeace concocted an “‘implausible story that this was a horrible accident”.

The defendant’s previous convictions included stabbing a man unknown to her to the jaw and neck in 2007.



The killer was also convicted of actual and grievous bodily harm, battery, affray, and assaulting a police officer.

Several of the convictions were against partners.

Makepeace was released from prison in 2021, and worked at a holiday park before becoming a manager at a shopping centre.

Senior Crown Prosecutor Rachel Worthington, of CPS Mersey-Cheshire, said: “Aurin Makepeace stabbed Steven Rothwell and then left him to die alone. She made no attempt to get any medical help for him.

“The reasons why she murdered him are known only to her. The jury have seen through Makepeace’s layers of lies.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The Crown Prosecution Service would like to thank the many witnesses in this case that have helped us bring Makepeace to justice for this brutal murder.

“The CPS would also like to take this opportunity to offer our condolences the family and friends of Mr Rothwell at this very difficult time.”

News.title: Paedo BBC producer GUILTY of sickening child sex offences after downloading 6,000 indecent images
News.content:
A PAEDO BBC producer has been found guilty of sickening child sex offences after downloading 6,000 indecent images.

Dylan Dawes, 50, made radio shows for stars including comedian Rhod Gilbert and Final Score host Jason Mohammad at the time of his crimes.





The fiend, who worked from BBC HQ in Cardiff, Wales, would leave his computer containing 6,200 child abuse images at his desk for “extended periods of time” where it was freely available to colleagues.

Dawes also made vile searches for terms including “jailbait” as he downloaded the pictures to laptop, hard drive, and two iPads.

Of the thousands of images, 192 were Category A – the worst kind.

After police discovered the twisted stash, Dawes claimed he had “no idea” where it had come from and even suggested his colleagues could be to blame in the “open-plan” BBC offices.

But jurors saw through his sick lies and he was today found three counts of possessing indecent images and three counts of making indecent images.

The court heard Dawes began working at the BBC in 2001 and had been downloading child abuse images between 2006 and 2022.

He worked for BBC Radio Wales as a producer before moving into a “content producing” role for the broadcaster’s website.

The dad-of-three was arrested in February 2022 after returning from a family holiday to Disneyland Paris.



He was taken for questioning at Cardiff Bay police station and answered a series of questions regarding his job and computers.

Dawes told the jury he was suspended on full pay following his arrest and was signed off sick with “stress”.

Following his arrest, the paedo producer denied possessing or making any indecent images of children.

He also said he had loaned an iPad to a colleague “for purely work-related purposes”.

At a second interview, Dawes gave police a prepared statement, saying: “I have no knowledge of any indecent images on my devices. I have never been in possession of any indecent images.



“I have never knowingly used, accessed, downloaded or sought indecent images of children. I have no sexual attraction to children.

“I have downloaded regular pornography with zip or jpegs. All devices have at times been left for extended periods in open plan offices.”

But Harry Baker, prosecuting, said the images had been found on four of Dawes’ devices and it was unlikely this was an “unhappy coincidence”.

Dawes, who is no longer employed by the broadcaster, will be sentenced on May 14.

News.title: At least one dead as tourist bus plunges down ravine on Canary Islands leaving 14 others injured
News.content:
HOLIDAY BUS SMASH At least one dead as tourist bus plunges down ravine on Canary Islands leaving 14 others injured

AT least one person has died and 14 others have been injured after a tourist bus plunged down a ravine in the Canary Islands.

Trapped passengers were rescued from inside the wreckage by emergency services who rushed to the scene with a helicopter, five ambulances and the fire brigade.





There were understood to be 24 adult passengers, one driver and three children on board the bus at the time of the tragedy.

Three people were “seriously injured” – although it is unclear whether this includes the driver or any of the minors.

Firefighters helped rescue efforts and prevented the bus from rolling further down the steep hill on the island of La Gomera.

The holiday hotspot is known for its picturesque landscapes – but also has very narrow roads spanning across high mountain points.

Local authorities said the crash happened at 1:15pm local time on the GM-2 near San Sebastián, the island’s most visited spot.

The site of the terrifying ordeal is near a mountain tunnel and a hazardous hairpin bend high above rocky terrain.

Emergency services said: “One person has died, three people are seriously injured and 11 others have suffered moderate injuries.

“The Canary Islands Emergency Service has sent to the scene of the accident a medicalized helicopter, five ambulances and a medical team including nurses.”



The nationalities of the passengers are currently unclear – and it is still unknown how or why the bus careered off the road.

The wounded victims have been rushed to La Gomera General Hospital.

But authorities are understood to be looking at transferring the most seriously injured passengers to hospitals in Tenerife.

The bus that crashed belongs to Gomera Tours, which offers excursions around the islands, as well as airport, port and hotel transfers.

La Gomera has a network of high and potentially dangerous roads.



Holidaymakers say driving down roads on the island is “like taking your life in your hands”.

The complicated landscape has also complicated rescue efforts, local authorities said.

They are currently probing the exact circumstances of the smash.

It comes after a 73-year-old woman died and 11 others were injured when a bus overturned on the exact same road and tumbled down a hill last May.

News.title: Travellers pave over field in ‘military op’ with diggers & chainsaws before angry lorry stand-off with villagers
News.content:
RESIDENTS in an idyllic village have raged against travellers who moved onto a plot of land in a “military-style operation” over the Easter weekend.

The small community has formed an association to put up opposition after travellers moved onto the field – causing traffic chaos and leaving residents furious.





Trucks, diggers and men using chainsaws launched a dawn operation on Good Friday moving tonnes of hardcore onto the hedged paddock.

The small community of Sundridge and Ide Hill, close to Sir Winston Churchill‘s wartime residence at Chartwell in Kent, was indignant at the activity over the bank holiday weekend.

Locals said trees in the field were cut down before a mobile home was brought onto the plot of land, causing traffic chaos on Sunday.



On Thursday, April 9, wooden fencing was put up on edge of the land with a wooden gate.

A boy in his teens could be seen painting the fencing with creosote.

On the site, a large mobile home, a caravan and a motorhome could be seen.

The people who moved onto the plot are understood to be a family of two parents and two young boys.



The plot of land was bought from the local parish council, who put it up for sale a property auction for £167,000 in the autumn.

On Tuesday, Sevenoaks District Council served them a Temporary Stop Notice (TSN) to prevent them making any more changes to the land until June.

In an update, the council addressed the “very challenging weekend”, saying: “We understand local people are concerned about the potential planning breach at Church Road.”

It added: “We will continue to visit the site frequently to record any changes and continue gathering evidence, which will be used to inform what actions are taken next.

“A further site visit has been conducted today due to new concerns raised by residents on an alleged breach to the TSN, which we are currently reviewing.”



Now, concerned locals have formed the Sundridge and Ide Hill Residents Association – which held a meeting on Easter Monday where more than 70 locals gathered to discuss the issue.

One local, who lives close to the site, said the operation began early on Good Friday morning.

She said: “First thing in the morning JCBs, earth moving vehicles, moved in and completely re-shaped the site. And by mid-morning we had lorry loads of hardcore coming back and forth.

“I believe there were about 30 tonnes delivered and spread all in about the space of one day. By the late afternoon, there was a motorhome in place on the prepared site.

“Further works continued on the Saturday and then early on the Sunday morning we were alerted to the fact there was a huge mobile home on its way up the road on the back of a lorry.



“They had blocked the road at the top to stop anyone coming down.”

Video footage from the village shows a huge lorry taking up the width of a small country lane.



This HGV has the mobile home on the back of it – now situated on the plot of land.

A group of three police officers can be seen observing the vehicle as it makes its way down the tiny road.

The woman said a group of concerned locals jumped in their cars and parked at the side of the road outside their houses, trying to impede the way for the lorry.

But, she said police insisted they must move their vehicles, though she said there are no parking restrictions on that street.

She continued: “They then facilitated safe passage up the road of this moving all the cars and people out of the way as it progressed – two men on the roof of the vehicle snapping off branches from trees.



“We should have had four days’ notice for a load of that size to come up the road.

“They should have had permission to bring it up here and permission to put it on the land.”

“The police took our numbers to check who we were but they didn’t take theirs. That road was blocked all day.”

The lorry made its way down the road with men stood on top of the roof of the mobile home, lopping down low-hanging branches from trees along the road with a chainsaw.

Furious locals were particularly angry with the conduct of the police, she added.



“The attitude of the police was absolutely shocking. They threatened to tow my car away,” she said. “They said they would take me away as well if I didn’t get out of the way.”

A Kent Police spokesperson said: “Kent Police was called to New Road in Sundridge near Sevenoaks shortly after 8am on Sunday 5 April 2026 to reports of a HGV becoming stuck and blocking the road.

“Patrols attended and discovered several cars were blocking the HGV, so the road was closed for officers to manage the situation.”

The police said the officers were working for hours to clear the road as a priority to maintain public safety.

Two drivers, including the lorry driver, were issued traffic offence reports.



A neighbour said they were shocked that the family was so brazen as to move in “secretively” during the Easter bank holiday weekend.

“They know what they’re doing,” the fuming local insisted.

Local MP Laura Trott expressed her frustration with the “unauthorised works” and called on the council to do more to tackle the problem.



On Saturday, she posted on social media: “I am afraid the unauthorised works continued on the site at the junction of Penn Lane yesterday, and with a caravan now in situ.

“I am incredibly disappointed and deeply frustrated to learn from the council that no action will be taken until Tuesday.

“Illegal developments must be shut down immediately, whether they occur over a bank holiday weekend or not.”

Trott added she would like to see planning law change to make it easier to refuse retroactive permission grants in such cases.

After the council issued the TSN, she issued an updated statement which read: “The council has this evening published an update setting out the full details of the case.



“They are currently investigating whether the Temporary Stop Notice has already been breached, and if that is the proven, criminal prosecutions must be initiated.”

A Council spokesman said: “Our planning team visited the site on several occasions over the Easter bank holiday weekend as part of our response to an alleged planning breach. We visited the site again on Tuesday 7 April before serving a Temporary Stop Notice later that evening.

“We are continuing to investigate the potential breach, and we have now received external legal advice. This will guide the legal and enforcement options open to us and our next steps.

“One family has moved onto the site, which they own. The site was previously owned by Sundridge Parish Council. Our enforcement action will be proportionate to any breach, taking account of Government guidance and legislation as well as local planning policies.”

Another resident, who lives close to the site, recalled: “There were loads of lorries going up and down and loads of hardcore.



“We went down there and suddenly there were lots of diggers and dumper trucks and a lot of hardcore went down.

“As soon as the last van went off the mobile home rolled on. I mean it was strategic in planning.”

He characterised the move as “a military-style operation”. He added: “They shouldn’t get away with it.”



He added: “The police were useless. Legally parked cars, they told people to move them because otherwise it would be obstruction.

“It was almost like the police escorted this thing in onto the site. There were guys on the roof with a chainsaw chopping branches. It wasn’t good and now we’ve got to deal with what we’ve got to deal with.”

This comes as it has emerged similar operations took place in other areas of the country over the Easter weekend.

Yesterday, The Sun reported yet another traveller site which had suddenly cropped up in a small village in Surrey.

There, locals were horrified as 21 caravans trooped onto the field where a large fence was also erected.



A Kent Police spokesperson elaborated on the traffic stand-off on Sunday: “A man in his 40s refused to follow police instructions and was arrested for obstructing a police officer. He was later released pending further enquiries.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Officers issued the driver of the lorry a traffic offence report for failing to have a tachograph installed. The driver of another vehicle was also issued a traffic offence report for careless driving.

“The road was cleared at around 4.30pm.”

News.title: Mystery as pregnant glam CEO and rapper Siditty, 36, is found shot dead inside $80,000 Range Rover as cops launch probe
News.content:
GUN TRAGEDY Mystery as pregnant glam CEO and rapper Siditty, 36, is found shot dead inside $80,000 Range Rover as cops launch probe

A GLAMOROUS CEO and rapper has been shot dead with cops finding her body inside an $80,000 Range Rover in mysterious circumstances.

Qualeisha Barnes, also known by her stage name Siditty, was 14 weeks pregnant when she was found dead in the front seat of her luxury SUV with police opening up a probe to find her killer.





The 36-year-old’s white Range Rover Sport was found in the middle of the street in Atlanta, Georgia at 1:30am on Wednesday.

The rapper’s body was inside with multiple gunshot wounds, the Fulton County Medical Examiner’s office confirmed.

Atlanta Police Department officials believe the unknown shooter most likely fired a weapon from outside the car before fleeing.



It remains unclear why the killer opened fire or if they knew the victim.

A suspect is yet to be named in the homicide case with cops scouring through CCTV footage from around the scene, local police said.

The investigation will also involves speaking to neighbors to see if can help come up with a possible motive, Lr. Christopher Butler told Atlanta News Now.

As well as being a rap artist, Barnes was also the CEO of an online retailer called So Siditty Boutique.



Her heartbroken family and friends have flooded social media with touching tributes since her untimely death was announced.

Cousin Monica Barnes said: “Life is not fair y’all didn’t have to do her like that. S.I.P Qualeisha Barnes A.K.A. So Siditty my blood cousin is gone lord jesus please keep my family in your prayers.'”

Another loved one posted: “Damn… I’m so sorry this happened to you… RIP cousin.”

Media company Detroit Got Talent also posted a heartfelt tribute saying: “Honoring the vibrant spirit of Detroit’s own SIDITTY, who touched so many lives. Your legacy will forever shine bright. Rest easy, queen.”

Barnes was well-known across her hometown in Detroit, Michigan.



At the time of her death she was in nursing school and was set to complete her degree in the coming months, her family said.

She had been living in Atlanta for around a decade.

Police chief Butler has now urged residents to contact the police through their anonymous tip line if they have any information which could lead to the capture of Barnes’ killer.

Investigators say anyone with information should come forward through Crime Stoppers Atlanta at 404-577-TIPS.

Butler also appealed to locals to review their home surveillance footage to see if anything can help with the investigation.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “Be vigilant, know your community, speak out if there’s something going on in your area.

“The community is our greatest asset.”

News.title: Inside Met Police’s £180k 4×4 SWAT vans seen patrolling London’s streets with bulletproof glass & blast-resistant armour
News.content:
HULKING bulletproof swat cars have been spotted on the streets of the capital as cops try out their new £180,000 toys.

The imposing 7ft 7in tall tank-like cars have been brought in to replace the aging fleet which prowled the streets during the infamous 2011 riots.





Their towering size, matte paint job and “POLICE” slogan emblazoned across the side of the cars makes them hard to miss.

Alarmed Londoners were reassured by the Met, though, that the cars were merely out on training drives – and not being used in operations.

A Metropolitan Police spokesman said the specialist vehicles were intended for use in only a few limited circumstances.

These were: high risk armed policing operations, for use by officers deployed at airports and as a contingency option for use in the most serious public disorder.

Its predecessor fleet was previously deployed solely for the most high-profile and serious police matters including riots and terrorist attacks.

The public may not see Plasan Sandcats out in the wild save for the most extreme public unrest and security threats.

The Met has invested somewhere in the region of £3.2million in the 18-strong armada from Israeli armoured vehicle company Plasan.



The mammoth 7,300kg 4x4s can transport up to 11 officers and stand at 7ft 7in tall.

Exact specifications for the cars purchased by the Met are not known, and the company’s armoured capabilities are also kept a secret.

But the Sandcat Mk4, tested by UK security forces back in 2021, boasts a Stanag Level 2 armoured rating – proofed against 7.62 calibre bullets, grenades, sniper rifles and AK47s.

It is built on a Ford F550 chassis, commonly used in tow trucks, but with a host of militaristic additions including strong bars on the front to punch through barricades, a roof hatch and the option to add weapon capabilities.

According to the company website, the Sandcat Tigris is the preferred choice for both the IDF and Ministry of Defence.



“They are a replacement for similar vehicles that have been in use for many years,” the Met spokesperson said.

“They will be on the roads more often in the coming months while we train officers to drive them, but they will not be used in a routine frontline policing environment and the vast majority of the public are unlikely to ever see them deployed operationally.”

Back in February, a fleet of the tank-like cars was spotted on the streets of Harrow, North West London.

The huge 4x4s were seen on training drives around the residential roads of the London suburb, Harrow Online reported.

The Met purchased 18 of the vehicles from a UK-based manufacturer last year to replace the older Jankel models.



The old fleet was most notably deployed during the 2011 riots, but have otherwise rarely been used.

They were also sent out to patrol the streets of the capital in a show of force after the horrific Westminster terror attack in 2017.

Bullet-resistant Jankel Guardians the force previously used cost about £100,000 each.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The seven-tonne personnel carrier could withstand AK-47 bullets and had a bomb-proof floor.

Known as “The Guardians”, the decommissioned fleet was used for 20 years before the sleek new Sandcats were brought in.

News.title: Killer FedEx driver’s alter ego says stripping Athena Strand, 7, was ‘funny’ in sick vid as last words to girl revealed
News.content:
HORRIFYING bodycam footage shows the FedEx delivery driver who murdered a seven-year-old girl switching between alter ego personalities.

Jurors watched the video in a Texas courtroom and heard details about how Athena Strand fought for her life in the back of the delivery truck before she was strangled to death and stripped naked.





Tanner Horner, 34, pleaded guilty to the kidnapping and murder of the Fort Worth girl, but claimed that his alter ego named “Zero” committed the killing on November 30, 2022.

He told cops he accidentally hit her with his van and that when he couldn’t calm her down, his other personality, “Zero”, took over.

Horner claimed that it was Zero who strangled her, stripped her naked and dumped her body in Trinity River, where she was found two days later.

Jurors are now determining whether he should receive the death penalty or life in prison without parole.



On Thursday, they were shown chilling bodycam footage of cops asking Horner where he disposed of her clothing after he killed her.

In the clip he switched to his ulterior personality and said he found the discarding of the child’s clothing “funny.”

“Are you saying you stripped her naked and threw her clothes out the window on the highway?” an officer is heard asking.



“I thought it was funny,” Horner replied.

“Did you take all her clothes off of her? Shirts, pants, panties – everything?” the officer asked.

“Mm-hmm,” the killed replied.

The officers then started addressing him as “Zero,” after finding him more receptive, and asked what she was wearing when he took her.

“No jacket, no shoes,” he replied.



“So did you hit her before you dropped the package? I’m sorry, did Tanner hit her before the package was dropped off, or after?” an officer said, as he tried to get a clear picture of what happened.

“Do you want to talk to him?” Horner replied, referring to himself.

“No, I want to talk to Zero. I want to talk to you. Because you’re being more honest, you’re more helpful,” the officer said.

When asked about the abduction, Horner claimed he told Athena they were “going for a ride” and denied that she tried to fight him.

Investigators have said that Horner repetedly changed his story and knew he was lying when questioned about removing her underwear.



Killer’s sick last words to Athena

As part of the trial, jurors have also been shown police interview footage of Horner recalling his last words to the girl before carrying out the brutal murder.

Chillingly, they likely offered her a glimmer of hope that she was going to survive.

“Just get in the back of the van, we’re going to the hospital,” he told investigators of their last exchange.

During this particular questioning, he denied he murdered the child.



As well as harrowing footage, jurors have listened to numerous testimonials including from Texas Ranger Job Espinoza, lead investigator.

He testified to the grim details of the case in court, noting Horner’s changing accounts of the murder.

Espinoza recalled asking Horner, “Did she scream?” to which he replied, “wasn’t able to.”

Another gruesome detail heard by the court was that Athena was likely sexually assaulted after cops found Horner’s DNA in “places where you shouldn’t find DNA on a seven-year-old girl.”

“I’m going to tell you right now. One thing you’re going to hear that is something you can’t unhear is the level of fight that a 7-year-old girl has. When she’s facing down a certain death,” Wise County District Attorney James Stainton told the court.



When asked by Espinoza if he was sorry for what he had done, Horner got emotional and said, “I’m a father.”

“All I want is to spend one last Christmas with my son, and I’ll tell you everything.”

His defense says he suffers from brain damage, mental illness, autism and extreme lead exposure.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The trial to determine Horner’s punishment is set to continue with more testimonies throughout the day on Friday.

A woman has also separately claimed Horner sexually assaulted her as a teenager in 2013, according to an arrest affidavit.

News.title: Britain’s most notorious prisoner Charles Bronson moved to Monster Mansion to rot alongside paedos & murderers
News.content:
Prison officers fear the long-time lag will 'kick off'

SHOCK SWITCH Britain’s most notorious prisoner Charles Bronson moved to Monster Mansion to rot alongside paedos & murderers

Britain’s most notorious inmate has been mysteriously moved to Monster Mansion as he makes a last-ditch bid to win his freedom.

Charles Bronson, 73, who has spent more than 50 years behind bars, was last week taken from Long Lartin near Evesham in Worcestershire to HMP Wakefield, which houses some of the country’s most dangerous men.





Prison officers at Wakefield are said to be “deeply worried” that Bronson will “kick off” after being placed back into solitary confinement at Cat A Wakefield and having his art equipment taken away.

A source told The Sun: “Everyone knows that Bronson hates Wakefield.

“The screws are really worried because everyone knows Bronson’s passion is painting and they’ve even taken away his pens and paints. There’s a concern he will kick off.

“Nobody can work out why he’s actually been moved though – it’s almost like it’s a deliberate attempt to get him riled up as he tries to persuade prison authorities to free him.”



Wakefield houses some of the country’s most twisted killers including Michael Sams, who murdered teenager Julie Dart, 18, in 1991 and later kidnapped estate agent Stephanie Slater.

Serial killer Robert Maudsley, who earned the nickname cannibal after allegedly eating part of another prisoner’s brain in a savage attack, is also an inmate.

Soham killer Ian Huntley, who murdered 10-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman in 2002, died this year after a brutal attack by a fellow lag in Wakefield.

Bronson, who goes by the surname Salvadore, was first jailed in 1974 for armed robbery but his sentence was increased to life after repeated violence and hostage-taking.



In 1997 Bronson held a deputy prison governor, staff and three inmates hostage and was given another five years. Two years after that he took an art teacher hostage for 44 hours at Hull prison.

The infamous felon has gone 12 years without a conviction and wants to be freed.

He is currently preparing for an oral hearing with prison authorities to try and secure his release after reports were drawn up by psychologists, probation staff and prison officers.



His lawyers had hoped that even if his parole is denied for the ninth time, Bronson would be downgraded to a lesser prison.

His ex-wife and confidant Irene Dunroe, who is in regular touch with Bronson, says she is appalled he’s been moved to Wakefield. She confirmed he has also had art equipment removed, despite Bronson becoming famous for his work.

Irene, 63, who refers to Bronson by his real name Mick Peterson, says: “They have moved him to the worst prison. Mick hates it there.

“They have put him in what they call the ‘cages’ again – it’s effectively a cell within a cell, underground. All the prisoners are either paedophiles or murderers.

“Mick is neither.”



She’s convinced prison authorities are trying to “ruffle his feathers” because Bronson has been on his best behaviour for the past few years.

She said: “What they are doing is stretching the elastic to see how far they can make it break….It’s disgusting.

“They’ve taken his art materials and given him just one pencil. This is because he’s nearing the oral hearing.

“They are supposed to be taking him out of solitary. This is so upsetting and stressful. The prison officials are the real criminals. It’s a disgrace.”



Monster Mansion HMP Wakefield earned its sinister nickname Monster Mansion because it houses some of the most evil prisoners in British history. The gruesome line-up included Soham killer Ian Huntley was was repeatedly hit around the head with a metal pole by a fellow inmate. He later died in hospital. The attack on Huntley has left other murderers and high profile perverts fearing for their lives. The Sun revealed how Sarah Everard’s sadistic killer Wayne Couzens, 53, is petrified of being targeted. Other inmates who are said to be scared include Urfan Sharif, who killed his daughter Sara, 10, and morgue monster David Fuller, 71, who was jailed for life in 2021 after sexually assaulting 101 female corpses.

A Ministry of Justice spokesman said: “We don’t comment on individual prisoners.

“The safety of our hard-working staff is our top priority, which is why we are increasing the use of mandatory body armour across the estate. It’s part of broader action we’re taking to boost safety, including more dog teams and better physical security measures.”

News.title: King and Queen commemorations for Queen Elizabeth II's 100th birthday revealed
News.content:
King and Queen commemorations for Queen Elizabeth II's 100th birthday revealed

Buckingham Palace has today revealed the involvement of members of the Royal Family during commemorations for the late Queen Elizabeth's centenary on April 21

View 4 Images Queen Elizabeth II stands with the then Prince of Wales, to watch a special flypast from Buckingham Palace balcony following the Queen's Birthday Parade, the Trooping the Colour, on June 2, 2022 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

King Charles and Queen Camilla will lead commemorations to the late Queen Elizabeth II to celebrate her 100th birthday later this month.

‌



On Monday, April 20, the King and Queen will visit the new Royal Collection Trust exhibition, Queen Elizabeth II: Her Life in Style, at The King’s Gallery, at Buckingham Palace. The biggest-ever exhibition of Elizabeth II's fashion, which is open until October, shows exactly how she made sure she lived up to her own words.

‌



Showcasing more than 300 pieces, including colourful dresses, hats, shoes, handbags and even a rare pair of trousers that belonged to the former monarch, nearly half of the items are being displayed for the public for the very first time. As exclusively revealed this week by The Mirror, the King will on Tuesday, April 21, deliver a rousing address to the nation to celebrate her life and legacy.

‌



View 4 Images King Charles will lead the nation in commemorations for the late Queen Elizabeth's 100th birthday on April 21 (Image: Getty Images)

King Charles will address nation on April 21 for Queen Elizabeth II’s 100th birthday READ MORE :

Charles, 77, is expected to convey what an inspiration his mother was not only to himself personally, but to the rest of the royal family. In the afternoon, Charles and Camilla, together with members of the Royal Family, will view the design recommendations for the Queen Elizabeth Memorial at the British Museum.

The Princess Royal will officially open The Queen Elizabeth II Garden in The Regent’s Park, London, during the afternoon. Later that day, the King and Queen, with other family members expected to include the Prince and Princess of Wales, will host a reception at Buckingham Palace to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the birth of Queen Elizabeth II.

‌



The reception will include dozens of representatives from the late Queen’s charities and organisations she was associated with during her 70 years on the throne. Elizabeth II became Britain's longest serving monarch on September 9, 2015, surpassing the record of 63 years, seven months, and two days, of her great-great-grandmother, Queen Victoria.

In 2022, the country celebrated the queen’s Platinum Jubilee, marking Elizabeth’s 70 year milestone on the throne. She passed away peacefully at her Balmoral home in Scotland on September 8, 2022, at the age of 96.

View 4 Images 'Queen Elizabeth II: Her Life in Style' is he largest exhibition of the Queen's fashion ever staged (Image: PA)

‌



As well as the King leading commemorations on the day, a range of engagements will also be held around the period to reflect both her 70-year reign and Elizabeth II’s cultural legacy. A national monument in St James’s Park in London has already been announced, with further details of final preparations expected soon, alongside other national memorial projects, cultural exhibitions, heritage openings and commemorative initiatives.

Key features of the winning design for the permanent national monument include a statue of the Queen in a new civic space called Queen Elizabeth II Place at Marlborough Gate, a new Prince Philip Gate on the other side of the park on Birdcage Walk with a statue of Philip, as well as a “family of gardens”, meandering paths and a new translucent, glass unity bridge.

After The Mirror exclusively revealed plans for the monument, Prime Minister Keir Starmer said it would provide “everyone with a place to honour the late Queen and connect with the shared history we cherish”. The memorial bridge is inspired by the tiara Queen Elizabeth wore on her wedding day to the late Prince Philip in 1947. The tiara, known as the Queen Mary Fringe diamond tiara, famously broke just hours before she was due to walk down the aisle.

‌



View 4 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales are expected to join commemorations to celebrate Queen Elizabeth II's 100th year later this month (Image: Getty Images)

The new crossing, located a stones throw away from the bronze statues on the Mall, will replace the park’s existing Blue Bridge and will serve as a fitting reminder of the late Queen’s achievements during her 70-year reign. A landmark exhibition called ‘Queen Elizabeth II: Her Life in Style’, announced yesterday, will welcome thousands of visitors to the King’s Gallery at Buckingham Palace until October 2026.

The specially curated exhibition will put on show for the first time the largest collection of the Queen’s outfits and personal belongings. A new commemorative garden is also opening in London’s Regent’s Park to honour her life and the Royal Mint will issue special £5 coins marking the centenary.

Article continues below

A royal source said: “The tone will not be somber, but rather a celebration and a chance for people across our four nations and the Commonwealth to come together and reflect on an amazing life and legacy of our late queen.”

News.title: 'We heard scratching coming from our walls and couldn't believe what was inside'
News.content:
'We heard scratching coming from our walls and couldn't believe what was inside'

A family in Leicester heard scratching noises coming from the walls of their garage on Easter Sunday and called firefighters, who rescued three fox cubs that had become trapped inside

View Image The family had their house wall broken down to get to the noise (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A family in Leicester found themselves on a rather unexpected Easter hunt this year, left completely puzzled by a mysterious noise coming from in-between the walls of their home.

‌



There are few things more unsettling than hearing a strange sound coming from inside your walls — particularly when you have no idea what might be lurking within. That was precisely the situation for one family, who called Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service on Easter Sunday, 5 April, to help get to the bottom of the peculiar noises. As it turned out, that call ended up saving three lives. Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service took to Facebook to share footage from the dramatic rescue, after crews discovered three tiny fox cubs trapped inside the walls of a residential garage.

‌



The fire service posted a series of pictures documenting the rescue, explaining that they had received a call from a member of the public after fox cubs were heard stuck between two buildings.

‌



"While you may have been on an Easter egg hunt on Sunday morning, one of our crews were busy cracking open a garage wall in a search for trapped fox cubs," the service said in the post.

With the homeowner's permission, firefighters carefully removed sections of brickwork from the garage wall before locating three young cubs wedged between the structures. What they uncovered, the service revealed, was "not one, not two, but three trapped cubs."

‌



One of the animals needed oxygen therapy, which crews provided using a specialist mask designed for small animals, the fire service explained.

Following the rescue, all three cubs were handed over to the local RSPCA animal charity branch for further care and treatment.

At the close of the post, the Fire Service urged people to 'never attempt' to rescue a distressed animal if it puts themselves at risk. Instead, they advised: "Always contact the appropriate animal rescue organisation."

‌



The footage has been watched over 142,000 times in just a couple of days, as viewers flocked to the comments section to applaud the efforts of both the fire service and the homeowners.

""That's a rescue with a difference!" one person wrote. Another said: "The most heartwarming thing I've read in ages! Well done.""

"Homeowner is a bit of a hero too," a third person said.

Article continues below

Leicestershire Wildlife Hospital also provided an update on the cubs: "An amazing rescue - thank you so much to all involved! And a big thank you to the RSPCA who brought the cubs over to us, and sought an overnight veterinary stay for one of them who was suffering from significant injuries (and is now very lucky to be alive!). The cubs are now in our care and being closely monitored."

If you're worried about an animal, whether domestic or wild, you can report your worries to the RSPCA via their website, where they will direct you to the quickest and most effective way to get help.

News.title: Family of teen musician hanged by Iran release his final haunting video
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Family of teen musician hanged by Iran release his final haunting video

The family of an 18-year-old musician has released the poignant final video he made before he was hanged by the Iranian regime which claimed he had tried to burn down a building

Outrage as Iranian regime executes teenage boy

The Iranian regime has been strongly criticised after it executed a teenage boy, amid fears the evil rulers will execute dozens more now that a two week ceasefire is in place.

‌



Amirhossein Hatami, 18, was hanged on Thursday after authorities in Tehran claimed he had tried to burn down a regime’s building. But his family and friends deny this, claiming he was just an aspiring musician protesting peacefully. They released an emotional video of Amirhossein singing. In it, the video mixes a lullaby whose words he has amended with the faces of six males and a female.

‌



It’s understood they were friends killed in the January uprisings when regime loyalists massacred thousands. Now he has been added to the list of the victims.

‌



View 5 Images Amirhossein's latest video features a lullaby amended with words he had written

One of the lyrics is: “Ah, our tears are nothing, our laughter is nothing "Our loss and gain are nothing "Only your embrace remains… everything else is nothing.”

Vahid Beheshti- a veteran hunger striker who is today still protesting outside the UK Foreign Office told the Mirror: “Amirhossein Hatami is a symbol of national resistance. “By killing him - and more in the last few days - they think that they can cause terror and fear in the population. But they're doing the opposite. “They're making the Iranian population even more angry, more likely to rise up. The regime is even more afraid of its own population than it is of American or Israeli bombs.

‌



View 5 Images Amirhossein's latest video features a lullaby amended with words he has written

“The regime is pretending to be strong but it is severely divided and may fall in days or weeks. They've lost almost everything - except the Western media. Amirhossein will become one of our country's many heroes.

Hatami’s mother also released a photo of him with his last birthday cake. On 18 January, state media aired the forced confessions of five of the defendants. In the video, they are referred to as “deceived youth” who were “directed by American-Zionist terrorist elements” to attack the IRGC base in Teheran.

‌



The revolutionary court's notorious Branch 15 was presided over by hardline judge Abolqasem Salavati - known as the "Judge of Death" for his long history of sentencing dissidents to execution or long jail terms.

View 5 Images The musician's mother released a photo of her son with his birthday cake

Salavati was sanctioned was in 2019 by the United States, and, earlier, by the European Union. Defence lawyers accused plainclothes forces of trapping protesters inside a building on January 8 during protests near a regime armed headquarters, run by the notorious Basij.

‌



They said the plainclothes men had locked the doors, and themselves started the fire. The court did not allow independent lawyers to defend the accused.

View 5 Images Protests against the US-Israel military action in Iran have taken place across the globe - including in the Phillippines (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

After being forced into videoed 'confessions', Hatami and six others were found guilty of 'Moharebeh' ('Enmity Against God'). On Thursday the judiciary announced he had been hanged at dawn.

‌



Two more protesters were hanged this week. Another nine prisoners are at risk of imminent execution over participating in the January protests. They had been subjected to torture and other ill-treatment in detention, Amnesty International said, before being convicted in "grossly unfair trials based on forced confessions".

On March 19, Iran executed 19-year-old Saleh Mohammadi, a wrestler who had taken part in international competitions. The court claimed he had helped kill three police officers during the nationwide protests. A vicious crackdown led to between ten thousand and 30 thousand protesters being shot dead, some while injured and lying in their hospital beds.

View 5 Images Government supporters in Iran gathered to mark the 40th day since the death of Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and his father, the slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei (Image: AP)

Article continues below

Amnesty International said it was "outraged". It said the execution showed the judiciary is "a tool of repression sending individuals to the gallows to spread fear and exacting revenge on those demanding fundamental political change".

Anti-regime organisations based in Europe say they believe over 100 more protesters will be sentenced to death and executed.

News.title: Brits reveal biggest everyday annoyances as queue jumpers top list
News.content:
Brits reveal biggest everyday annoyances as queue jumpers top list

Brits have revealed the the small things that irritate them the most, with forgetting about a cup of tea until it goes cold, stubbing a toe and chipping a nail also on the list

Gladiator's Nitro speaks to the public about their annoyances

Brits' top daily irritations include queue jumpers, noisy eaters and the struggle to open jars. A survey of 2,000 adults unveiled the minor things that vex them the most, with forgetting about a cuppa until it goes cold, stubbing a toe and chipping a nail also making the list. An additional 15% are frustrated by cryptic social media posts, and a whopping 43% get angered by lateness.

‌



Everyday tasks like hanging up picture frames that end up crooked annoy 11%. Other day to day activities people find annoying are waiting for a bus or train to arrive only for it to turn up late (35%) and opening tin cans (9%).

‌



View 2 Images Brits have revealed the small things that frustrate them most (Image: Simon Jacobs/PinPep / SWNS)

‌



When tackling tasks like these, 9% confessed their patience only lasts up to five minutes before they hit their limit. It also transpired one in four will make just three attempts at a challenging practical task before losing patience and giving up.

Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, also known as Nitro from Gladiators, hit the streets with Chupa Chups to find out more about the nation's irritations.

He said: "It's the little things that can test your patience the most. Getting out and about to chat to the public I saw it first hand; you train for big moments but no one trains for a jar that won't budge or a lollipop wrapper that just won't open – it can be humbling.

‌



"But what surprised me most is how universal it all is. We're all dealing with small frustrations, day in, day out and while we can't control everything, making even the smallest things easier can genuinely lift your mood and keep your day moving."

The study also found a quarter of those polled find themselves irritated by minor inconveniences, particularly when they're already tired (39%), running late (33%) or hungry (21%). For 31%, public transport leads the way as a hotspot for frustration, with supermarkets and their homes also ranking highly as places they're likely to be faced with disruptions.

Even tasks like opening food packaging winds up more than a third (35%) and unwrapping lollipops was considered a challenging task by 43%.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Aikines-Aryeetey spoke to the public about their biggest irks (Image: Simon Jacobs/PinPep / SWNS)

On the positive side, 52% are likely to seek resolutions to avoid annoyance and save themselves time, and for 17% it's simply about trying something new.

With some of the top hacks including using scissors to cut pizza (20%), wearing gloves to open jars (23%) and microwaving cold tea (24%).

‌



Kim McMahon from Chupa Chups, which commissioned the research to mark the launch of its new easier to open wrapper, said: "I'm sure we can all relate to these everyday annoyances, it's surprising how something seemingly small can have a big impact on our moods.

"It felt natural to tap into this topic for us given the well-known struggles with lollipop packaging and consumers getting openly frustrated on social media. Saving a moment or two can really impact your overall day or even week."

26 THINGS THAT REALLY ANNOY THE BRITISH PUBLIC:

Queue jumping People chewing loudly when they eat People playing videos loudly without headphones People being late People putting their feet on public transport seating People that walk slowly People shouting unnecessarily down the phone When you spill something on newly washed clothes Public transport being late Stubbing your toe People eating smelly foods in public spaces e.g. tuna sandwich in train station People leaving the toilet seat up When you drop and subsequently break bowls/plates When your tea is cold by the time you drink it Phone unexpectedly runs out of charge When a subscription fee unexpectedly comes out your account Bin men blocking the road When you chip a nail Cryptic social media posts People not loading the dishwasher properly When you hang up a picture frame and it goes wonky People who don’t wipe down the gym equipment after using it Opening jars Being caught off guard with milk beyond its best-before date Big bags on the tube/train Opening tins

News.title: Jet2 issues message as some passengers may need 'letter of authorisation'
News.content:
Jet2 issues message as some passengers may need 'letter of authorisation'

Some countries require certain passengers to have a specific document and those travelling without it might be turned away

View 3 Images Portugal is a popular holiday destination (Image: Getty)

Jet2 has issued guidance about passengers who are aged 14, sharing that certain passengers may be required to carry additional documentation when travelling.

‌



The airline notes: "Jet2.com allows passengers aged 14 or over to travel alone. Any passenger under the age of 14 can only travel if accompanied by a passenger aged 16 years or over who will take full responsibility for them. We are unable to offer an ‘Unaccompanied Minors’ service."

‌



Talking about travelling with children, it also notes that while it allows people who are 14 and over to travel alone, "some countries impose special conditions for minors who are travelling either alone, or without their legal parent/guardian."

‌



View 3 Images You may need an extra document with you (Image: Getty)

For example, if you have a child who is travelling to Portugal, they may need a letter. GOV.UK confirm "children aged 17 and under travelling to Portugal alone, or with a person who is not their parent or legal guardian, must carry a letter of authorisation to travel from their parent or guardian, together with a copy of their parent or guardian’s passport."

Make sure the letter includes:

‌



the child’s full name, date of birth and passport number

the child’s dates of arrival and departure

the name of the adult in Portugal who will be responsible for them during their stay

the full names, dates of birth, passport numbers and contact details of the parent or guardian

the parent or guardian’s signature and date of issue

a copy of the parent or guardian’s passport

It adds: "If you bring a child to Portugal without a letter of authorisation, your entry will be delayed and may be refused.

"Teenagers aged 17 and under who travel alone, or with friends of the same age, and who are not being met on arrival by a parent or guardian, may be refused entry if they do not have a letter of authorisation."

‌



Jet2 continue: "To avoid delays at the border, we recommend a copy of the signatories’ (parent or legal guardian) photo identification is carried with the young person for verification purposes, by the authorities at the Portuguese border."

Non-resident children leaving Portugal

Non-resident children aged 17 or under leaving Portugal without a parent or legal guardian, or accompanied by someone else, must have an authorisation letter, unless they are travelling back to their country of residence.

‌



Resident children leaving Portugal

View 3 Images No matter which airline you fly with, make sure you check your luggage meets their rules (Image: Getty)

A child aged 17 or under who resides in Portugal must have a duly certified authorisation letter when travelling without a parent or legal guardian. See more details in the Living in Portugal guide.

Article continues below

Jet2 luggage tip - write this on your tag

People travelling with the airline have been urged to take extra care when checking in their luggage. On its website, on a page called Top Tips before Travel, the airline encouraged passengers to follow its "top baggage tips for a smooth journey".

One tip is to label your bags with three key pieces of information. As we previously reported, it suggests: "Label each piece of baggage with your name, flight number, and phone number."

News.title: Grand National 2026: Gold Dancer dies after suffering fatal injury while winning race
News.content:
Gold Dancer has sadly died after picking up a fatal injury en route to victory in the William Hill Mildmay Novices' Chase at Aintree. The seven-year-old ran an almost perfect race and was on course for a wide-margin win before stumbling at the final fence.

The Willie Mullins-trained horse still managed to record a near five-length win but sad scenes unfolded at Aintree as the horse limped across the line before being dismounted quickly by Paul Townend. Vets attended to the horse as screens were brought on before the worst possible news was confirmed.

"He’s been put down. He broke his back," said Eddie O'Leary, racing manager for the Gigginstown stable. "It’s terribly sad for the horse. What could Paul Townend do? He felt fine, it was just when he pulled up that something was wrong."

Miami Magic and Jordans Cross fell during the race but ITV confirmed both horses had walked back to the stables afterwards.

‌



Grand National 2026 results from every race on Ladies Day at Aintree READ MORE :

Aintree Racecourse issued a statement confirming the news. They said: "The winner of our second race of the day, Gold Dancer, was pulled up after the line and dismounted.

"He was immediately attended to by our expert veterinary team but sadly he could not be saved. Our heartfelt condolences are with his connections."

ITV presenter Ed Chamberlin added: "The winner was immediately attended by veterinary team but sadly could not be saved."

The Jockey Club - who own 15 racecourses in the UK and the organiser of both the Cheltenham and Aintree Festivals - continue to work to minimise risks in the sport.

‌



Emma Slawinski, chief executive at the League Against Cruel Sports, said: “Year after year we see horses dying at Aintree for people’s entertainment and a cheap bet. Sadly, Gold Dancer is the latest victim of this heartless spectacle which flies in the face of animal welfare."

Gold Dancer finished second in the Jack Richards Novices' Limited Handicap Chase at the Cheltenham Festival in March. He'd previously been a winner at Tipperary and Galway in Ireland for Mullins, having began his racing career in France.

Regent's Stroll finished second in the 2:20 at Aintree, with Salver finishing third.

News.title: GP explains little-known reason it's vital to have clean headlights in April
News.content:
GP explains little-known reason it's vital to have clean headlights in April

Two-thirds of people have said they have problems driving in the spring compared to some other seasons

View 3 Images It is important to have clean headlights (Image: Getty)

While spring brings with it warmer weather and longer daylight hours, it’s also a season where it’s wise to be wary when you’re behind the wheel. New research has found that two-thirds (64%) of Brits say their eyes feel more tired during the spring months of the year.

‌



Dr Nisa Aslam, advisor to MacuShield, specialists in eye supplements, explains why. She says: “Driving places extra demands on our vision when there are low light levels of light and indeed bright light that can fall into a windscreen and cause glare; glare from headlights, rain and generally poor weather conditions, which all make it harder for the eyes to focus quickly and clearly.”

‌



Tired eyes during spring are caused by a combination of risk factors such as increased screen time as we still stay indoors more; reduced daylight hours versus the longer hours of summer and dry indoor air. This is causing a third (33%) of Brits to notice blurry vision and just over one in four say they have dry or irritated eyes during the winter into spring months.

‌



View 3 Images Dr Nisa Aslam has explained why headlights can be a problem (Image: Dr Nisa Aslam)

Dr Aslam adds: "Coupled with this, many of us tend to change our diets across the winter and spring seasons which often lack the correct eye-supporting nutrients." The expert has now identified four things that can help tired spring eyes when it comes to driving.

‌



Avoid driving when tired

With so many Brits experiencing tired eyes during spring, being physically tired may only make things worse. “Avoid driving when you’re tired and if you’re driving long distances, take regular breaks as tired eyes react more slowly, especially in poor light,” says Dr Aslam.

Eat the rainbow, every day

Dr Aslam says: "Eye health-supporting nutrients include vitamin B2, copper, vitamin C and macular carotenoids- lutein, meso-zeaxanthin and zeaxanthin - these form the macular pigment, the central part of the retina in the eye which is responsible for sharp, detailed vision.”

View 3 Images People are urged to 'eat the rainbow' (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

She advises people should eat a range of colourful fruit and veg and consider a supplement to help bridge any dietary gaps such as MacuShield Original+Omega 3 which contains a nutrient blend of the three macular carotenoids plus vitamin B2 and a daily dose of 250mg of DHA – which each help to maintain normal vision.

Check your headlights

Before you set of on a drive, especially in dim light, give your car a quick once-over. Dr Aslam says: “Ensure headlights are clean and properly aligned to avoid unnecessary glare. Lower the dashboard brightness at night too; this helps reduce the strain on your eyes. Make sure your windscreen and mirrors are clean and use anti-glare settings.”

Eat oily fish at least once a week

Dr Aslam explains: “The omega-3 fatty acid Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is of particular benefit for eyes, as the cell membranes of the retina contain a high concentration of DHA. We need 250 milligrams (mg) of DHA daily to help to maintain normal vision.” DHA is found in oily fish such as sardines, mackerel and salmon 11 .

News.title: 'I moved from UK to France for a better life but there's one issue I didn't see coming'
News.content:
'I moved from UK to France for a better life but there's one issue I didn't see coming'

Debbie Dawtrey moved from Cambridgeshire to south-western France in 2023 and opened a hotel, but she's found that one of the most significant problems has been difficult to overcome

View 4 Images Debbie runs a small hotel in the picturesque village of Confolens (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Many of us dream about relocating to some idyllic corner of Europe to soak up the sun and embrace the advantages of Mediterranean living. However, beyond the complications of European red tape – and the considerable cost – there's another significant obstacle that numerous people fail to consider.

‌



Debbie Dawtrey, who relocated from Buckden in Cambridgeshire to south-western France in 2023, reveals that one of the most substantial challenges she's faced is feeling socially cut off.

‌



Debbie, 64, established a boutique hotel in the Charente, situated in the charming village of Confolens, and explains that while she remains extremely occupied throughout the tourist season, the colder months can prove incredibly isolating.

‌



She told The Times: "I didn't know anyone in the area and while the summers are busy with guests, contacts are transient and the winters are especially hard as people hunker down and close the shutters."

Debbie, who is unmarried, explains she's discovered a method of reconstructing her social connections by arranging a monthly supper club for fellow expats: "Every month we'd take turns in hosting a dinner and had lots of fun," she explains, "it helped broaden our social circle."

View 4 Images Debbie organises regular meals for fellow ex-pats (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Debbie emphasises that becoming isolated is remarkably easy when relocating far from relatives and friends, and recommends "you have to really make an effort to put yourself out there".

Even when you've attempted to master the native tongue, the capacity to initiate spontaneous conversations can prove far more challenging than forming friendships back in Britain.

While some individuals might frequent a neighbourhood pub, or perhaps become members of a fitness centre, these are more readily available in bigger towns and cities. Establishing a fresh existence in the French countryside – or indeed in a remote UK community, can prove quite demanding.

‌



Even those working with substantial financial resources can find themselves yearning for what they've left behind. Earlier this year, Kate Ferdinand spoke candidly about her homesickness following her relocation to Dubai with her footballer husband Rio.

View 4 Images Kate Ferdinand admitted that she has struggled after emigrating (Image: Cedric Ribeiro/Getty Images for Atlantis The Royal/ Dolce&Gabbana x Ounass)

On her 'Blended' podcast in February, Kate became emotional and confessed she was pining for her family and friends back home. Kate and Rio relocated to the UAE last August and while her husband is "loving" his new existence there, matters aren't quite as positive for Kate.

‌



"I am enjoying it, but I miss home quite a lot," she acknowledged. "I can't talk about it because I get upset. I feel like we've opened our eyes to a different world. But I love London. I do feel happy in Dubai, but I'm just missing a part of me."

A source close to the pair told The Mirror that the Dubai move hasn't turned out as Kate had anticipated, and she considers the gleaming Middle Eastern metropolis "soulless."

View 4 Images Kate and Rio Ferdinand (Image: Mirror)

Article continues below

They revealed: "She's struggling. She's really missing home. She's not enjoying it. And even though she's got the kids and she's got Rio there, she's homesick. She can't stop it and it's very difficult. It's just not home." Kate is also feeling the absence of her stepsons. While Rio's daughter Tia, 14, made the transition to the UAE alongside the family, his elder sons Lorenz, 19, and Tate, 17, stayed behind in the UK to pursue their promising football careers – a decision that has caused Kate considerable heartache.

Opening up on her podcast, she admitted: "I miss the big boys a lot and I'm struggling with that. I know this decision is right for my younger children and as a family we are settled there, but the boys are following their football careers. So they're doing what they want to do, otherwise they'd be with us."

She went on to say: "But it's very hard because we've been through so much as a family and we've always been together and that's a huge adjustment."

News.title: LeBron and Bronny James record first son-to-father assist in NBA history
News.content:
Bronny James passed to parent LeBron for the first son-to-father assist in NBA history as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Golden State Warriors 119-103.

Bronny, 19, stole possession and passed to LeBron, who ran the length of the court for an uncontested dunk that was part of a 26-point contribution from the 41-year-old.

The pair recorded the first father-to-son assist in a match against the Brooklyn Nets last month.

LeBron also added 11 assists while Bronny scored 10 points with three assists as the Lakers saw off their state rivals.

The Lakers sit fourth in the Western Conference while the Warriors are in 10th, with both having already qualified for the post-season play-offs that begin on 18 April.

Elsewhere, the New York Knicks won 112-106 against the Boston Celtics, with Josh Hart scoring 26 points, to put pressure on their opponents in the Eastern Conference.

The sides are third and second respectively in the standings, with two matches left to play in the regular season.

The Toronto Raptors triumphed 128-114 against the Miami Heat while the Houston Rockets won 113-102 against Philadelphia 76ers to solidify their chances of a play-off place.

News.title: Simple guide: How the Iran war is affecting the cost of holidays, food and clothes
News.content:
By-products from petrochemicals are used to produce drugs including painkillers, antibiotics and vaccines.



The UK imports most of its generic medicines, with 30% coming from India, which in turn depends on the Gulf to supply a significant proportion of its crude oil imports.



The UK was experiencing some product shortages before the war, and recently NHS leaders and pharmacies raised concerns about supplies and prices. Last week the government said it wasn’t aware of any supply issues caused by the conflict.



The National Pharmacy Association says the war has pushed up the cost of transporting and manufacturing some medicines.



Some pharmacies say they’ve increased the cost to customers of common generic over-the-counter medicines, such as paracetamol and hay fever treatments, by about a fifth.



The NPA says some wholesale prices for pharmacies ordering in stock have almost doubled since the start of the war, and it anticipates more of these extra costs will be passed on to patients in the coming weeks.



There won’t be a change to how much people pay for their prescriptions, it says, as these prices are fixed by the NHS.

To snap or not to snap – that is the question: Lesley Manville has ignited an impassioned debate after criticising “insulting” theatregoers who take photos during curtain calls.

According to the Olivier Award-winning star, she believes phones should be kept in pockets until after the cast have given their bows to an applauding audience.

Manville, who currently stars in Les Liaisons Dangereuses at the National Theatre, urged people to “take the digital out of it for just a moment”, stating: “Come on, it’s theatre – let’s preserve it!”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville urges theatregoers to leave phones in their pockets during curtain calls ( Getty )

“We are all in this room, we are telling you a story, you’re listening – clap or don’t clap, but don’t just stick your phone in our face,” she said on Radio 4.

The Phantom Thread actor, 70, said it stems from people “wanting to prove they’ve seen” a production, but wondered why they “can’t let it live in their souls for five minutes”.

Manville noted it was particularly an issue on Broadway, saying that “virtually the whole audience will take their phones out at the end of the evening”, and has now noticed it “starting to filter in” to the West End, where it “never used to happen”.

There are some productions – including Six, the comedy musical about the lives of Henry VIII’s wives – where photos, and even filming, during the curtain call are encouraged. Some musical theatre stars, including Legally Blonde’s Amber Davies, regularly reshare footage from audience members posted on Instagram.

However, the expected etiquette in plays can be different. Manville’s Les Liaisons Dangereuses notes at the beginning that photos are not permitted during the curtain call, which might lead audience members to believe it’s OK to take out their phones when there is no disclaimer ahead of the show.

Manville’s comments have ignited a debate, with many wading in to share their views on the subject. The actor isn’t alone in her opinion, with Hannah Waddingham writing in response to her comments: “HEAR HEAR Lesley Manville.”

However, many others supported the idea of taking photos during the curtain call, including former Strictly Come Dancing professional Oti Mabuse, who suggested that an audience member’s photo may have more of a lasting impact for that person than the actors realise.

“I get her argument, but theatres nowadays is so expensive – if a family has travelled far and saved up every last bit of their money to come to the theatre to enjoy and this is their first or very last time, that one picture will make their absolute life!” she said.

“They get to keep that moment on their device for a lifetime. That photo could be the difference of keeping the dream alive for a little kid and having them simply forget.”

open image in gallery Oti Mabuse thinks photos during curtain calls could be ‘life changing’ for audience member ( PA )

Mabuse added that, when she watched her first show, she took photos of lead star Beverley Knight – and it was having that photo that inspired her to pursue her dreams. “If I didn’t have her as my screensaver for a year, my life would have turned out differently!” she wrote. That was the year she became a dancer on Strictly.

Loose Women star Denise Welch said that taking photos “of a fabulous audience reaction is something you can share with friends, not just social media”, stating: “I'd love to see a standing ovation being celebrated for something I'd worked really hard for.”

Theatre performer Ali McGregor said she “disagrees strongly” with Manville’s view – especially as people posting about shows can help with promotion.

“I would never take a photo during the performance, but taking a photo of the curtain call is a respectful way to take a photo for socials. It doesn’t take away from me sitting in the moment, doesn’t bother the rest of the audience’s enjoyment. I find this an extraordinary thing to complain about.”

Islamabad entered a state of lockdown on Friday as Pakistan’s capital prepared to host high-stakes negotiations to end the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Army and paramilitary personnel guarded the roads around Serena Hotel, the venue of the talks, as police beefed up security across the city. On Wednesday, the luxury hotel’s management had asked its guests to check out by 5pm as the government had requisitioned the property for an “important event from this evening until Sunday”.

Pakistan’s political and military leaders achieved a major diplomatic breakthrough by mediating a ceasefire between the US and Iran early on Wednesday. The ceasefire was declared less than two hours before the deadline on US president Donald Trump’s threat to obliterate a “whole civilisation” if Iran did not open the Strait of Hormuz, a critical maritime route that usually carries a fifth of the global supply of oil and gas.

Although the truce was immediately threatened by Israel’s deadly strikes on Lebanon which killed hundreds of people, it paved the way for American and Iranian diplomats to gather in Pakistan and negotiate an end to nearly six weeks of intense fighting.

open image in gallery Pakistani soldiers arrive for deployment at the Red Zone in Islamabad ( AFP via Getty )

The diplomats will be under great pressure to pull off what some analysts are describing as “mission impossible” – a deal that brings peace to the Middle East and stabilises a world economy battered by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

In preparation for the meeting, the government declared public holidays on Thursday and Friday while police imposed strict traffic restrictions in Islamabad.

“The Red Zone and surrounding areas are closed to all types of traffic except official vehicles. Citizens are requested to avoid unnecessary travel,” the city police said in an advisory.

The Red Zone is a city landmark housing key government offices and foreign missions.

open image in gallery An army truck drives past Serena Hotel in Islamabad ( AFP via Getty )

The heightened security measures are informed by the threat of terrorism, which remains real and present. There was a suicide bombing in Islamabad as recently as February and it was one of the triggers for the Pakistani airstrikes that fuelled weeks of fighting with neighbouring Afghanistan.

Islamabad accuses the neighbouring country of sheltering Islamist and ethnic insurgents responsible for carrying out terror attacks on its soil. Kabul denies the allegations.

“Given those risks, the lack of preparation time and the high-profile nature of these talks, this is a very challenging visit from a security perspective and speaks to the importance this administration places ⁠on the negotiations,” Elizabeth Threlkeld, director of the South Asia Program at the Stimson Center, said.

open image in gallery A view of the Red Zone in Islamabad ( AFP via Getty )

The US is expected to send a delegation headed by vice president JD Vance to conduct the talks in Islamabad, while Iran is set to be represented by foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

Gulf nations such as Qatar and Saudi Arabia, both of which are parties to the conflict, may also send delegations to Islamabad and hold talks on the sidelines.

open image in gallery A Pakistani army helicopter flies over Islamabad ahead of the talks between the US and Iran ( AFP via Getty )

Pakistani interior minister Mohsin Naqvi assured US chargé d’affaires Natalie Baker of elaborate arrangements for the visiting diplomats.

The newspaper Dawn reported that a 30-member US team was already in Islamabad to assess the security preparations.

Security analyst Zahid Hussain said the challenge for Pakistan was not just protecting the venue but to prevent diplomacy from being overtaken by forces outside the room.

Aside from this, analysts say, there isn’t much Pakistan can do. “What it lacks is meaningful leverage to compel ​concessions if the US and Iran are not willing to come to terms," Ms Threlkeld said.

News.title: JD Vance issues warning to Iran as he heads to Islamabad for peace talks
News.content:
US Vice President JD Vance issued a warning to Tehran as he sets off for crucial negotiations between the US and Iran in Islamabad.

“We’re looking forward to negotiation. I think it's going to be positive,” Vance said Friday. “As the president of the United States said, if the Iranians are willing to negotiate in good faith, we're certainly willing to extend the open hand.

“If they're going to try to play us, then they're going to find the negotiating team is not that receptive,” he added. “So we're going to try to have a positive negotiation. The president gave us some pretty clear guidelines, and we're going to see.”

It comes after Trump accused Iran of doing a “dishonourable” job after the ceasefire by failing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Experts told The Independent that passage through the shipping route largely remains at a standstill.
